## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Changes are needed before merge: deleting the defaults file breaks `load_defaults()`, and the new helpers contain a boundary error and silent configuration failures. Tests were inspected without execution.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — Deleting this file makes `app.startup.load_defaults()` raise `FileNotFoundError`, because it still reads the sibling `defaults.json`; please retain the file or update its loader. — Every call to load the application defaults now fails.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — `is_valid_port(65535)` returns `False`, although the documented range includes 65535; please use `0 < p <= 65535`. — Callers reject a valid TCP port.
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — Loading a config containing `{"timeout":` swallows the JSON parsing exception and returns `{}` without a diagnostic or documented fallback behavior; please propagate an actionable error identifying the path. — Callers cannot distinguish malformed configuration from a successfully loaded empty object.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — The docstring promises “returns None when h is empty,” but the empty-input branch executes `return ""`; please align the documentation and behavior. — Callers following the documented contract and checking `is None` miss empty hosts.
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — The trailing-dot branch has no test: the existing host test only passes `"Example.COM"`; please assert that `normalize_host("Example.COM.")` returns `"example.com"`. — A regression that preserves the terminal dot would pass the existing tests.

## Strengths
- The milliseconds test checks that `"1500ms"` produces `1.5`, verifying preservation of fractional seconds.
- Configuration loading is tested with an actual temporary JSON file and an assertion on the parsed result.
